explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1051 up to a harmless generalisation: a is a strictly increasing ℤ-valued sequence, without the page's 1 ≤ a_1. Negative terms only add finitely many rational summands. A zero term a_k = 0 makes Lean drop the two terms adjacent to it (division by zero gives 0), but the remaining tail is again a positive sequence of the same type: the growth condition is shift-invariant, since liminf of a_{n+m}^{1/2^n} > 1 iff liminf of a_n^{1/2^n} > 1. So the Lean statement is still true and equivalent in substance. Taking the liminf in EReal correctly covers the case liminf = ∞, and indexing from 0 rather than 1 does not matter.
